items.title: Leisure and Hospitality Leads U.S. Job Growth on World Cup Boost
items.summary: While it's not clear the World Cup's tourism impact will live up to the hype, federal data shows the hospitality sector is staffing up ahead of the tournament.

items.title: The Verdict: Travel’s AI Race Has an Operating Problem
items.summary: We heard from more than two dozen of travel's most important tech leaders — the people actually deploying AI solutions every day. Here's what the industry still needs to get right.

items.title: Ixigo Acquires Hotel Booking Platform and Invests in AI Startups
items.summary: With Brevistay, Ixigo closes the last major gap in its travel stack. Its twin bets on AI infrastructure hint at a larger goal of keeping trip planning inside its ecosystem, rather than letting it migrate to ChatGPT.

items.title: Amsterdam Proposes Tourism Tax Hike to 20%
items.summary: Raising taxes is easy — actually reducing visitor numbers is the problem Amsterdam hasn't solved.

items.title: Connectivity Is Becoming Travel’s Most Critical Trust Signal
items.summary: Connectivity has become a foundational layer of the travel experience. As the smartphone becomes the control point for travel, reliable connection is becoming less about convenience and more about trust.

items.title: The Two-Sided AI Squeeze That Only Travel Faces
items.summary: Travel is the only major industry getting hit from both directions at once: AI search volumes are exploding without converting while total AI token bills internally are rising.

items.title: Accor CEO Bazin’s Final Stretch: An AI Warning and What’s Next for Ennismore
items.summary: CEO Sébastien Bazin said an Ennismore IPO is "one of four or five" possible fates for the lifestyle joint venture. In M&A-speak, that means Accor's board hasn't decided yet.
